# epidemia (Python)

> Bayesian semi-mechanistic renewal-process modelling of infectious diseases, in
> PyMC + nutpie. A Python counterpart of the R package `epidemia`
> (https://mlgh-sg.com/epidemia2/).

Latent daily infections follow a discrete renewal process (a self-exciting point
process). The time-varying reproduction number `R_t` is a non-centred random walk
on the link scale; observations are a causal delay/ascertainment convolution of
infections. Models are specified in PyMC and fit with nutpie (a fast Rust NUTS
with Fisher-information mass-matrix adaptation), returning an ArviZ
`InferenceData`.

## Docs

- [Home, install, quick start](index.md): install with `uv`; a minimal end-to-end fit.
- [User guide](guide.md): model structure (transmission / infections / observations), `EpiConfig` options, `fit` arguments, plotting, and the performance design (what is vectorised vs. an irreducible sequential scan).
- [API reference](reference.md): full public API — `EpiConfig`, `build_model`, `fit`, `renewal`, `data`, `plots`.
- [Full docs, single file](llms-full.txt): all of the above concatenated for LLM ingestion.

## Running the code

- Install: `cd python && uv sync` (numba CPU backend; works on Apple Silicon). GPU on Linux: `uv sync --extra gpu` then `epi.fit(..., backend="jax")`.
- Minimal fit:
  ```python
  import numpy as np, epidemia as epi
  d = epi.flu1918()
  y = np.concatenate([[np.nan], d.incidence])
  config = epi.EpiConfig(gen=d.generation, i2o=np.repeat(0.25, 4), seed_days=6,
                         link="log", family="neg_binom",
                         intercept_loc=np.log(2.0), intercept_scale=0.2, rw_prior_scale=0.1)
  idata = epi.fit(y, config, draws=1000, tune=1000, chains=4)
  ```
- Packaged example: `uv run epidemia-flu --save flu`.
- Posterior contains latent series `Rt`, `infections`, `E_obs`; plot with `epi.plots.plot_rt(idata)`, `plot_infections`, `plot_obs(idata, observed=y)`.

## Key model facts

- Renewal: `i_t = R_t * sum_s gen[s-1] * i_{t-s}`, seeded over `seed_days`.
- Transmission: `R_t = link^{-1}(intercept + cumsum(rw_scale * rw_noise))`, non-centred (avoids the funnel / divergences). Links: `"log"` or `("scaled_logit", K)`.
- Observations: `E_t = sum_k i2o[k] * i_{t-k}`; families `"poisson"`, `"neg_binom"` (default), `"normal"`.

## Bundled data

- `epi.europe_covid()`, `epi.europe_covid2()` — 11 European countries, first
  COVID-19 wave: cases/deaths, five NPI indicators, `si`, `inf2death`.
- `epi.england_b117()` — SGTF-split English case counts behind Volz et al.
  (2021), *Nature* 593:266-269. 49 areas x 120 days, plus `pop`, `iar`,
  `iar_sd`, `i2o`, **and the paper's own fitted estimates** (`published`,
  `published_england`) so a reproduction can check itself.

## Delay-kernel convention (important)

Both `gen` and `i2o` are **lag-1-first**: entry 0 weights infections one day
back, and an infection is never observed on the day it happens. Entry *k*
(1-based) carries the mass in **(k-1, k]**, so a kernel's mean lag sits half a
day above its distribution's mean and no mass falls at lag 0.

Reproductions should **build their own kernel** rather than use a bundled one:
Flaxman et al. discretise at the midpoint (half a day different), and the
B.1.1.7 model's `i2o` sums to **7, not 1** because its observations are weekly
totals attached to a daily series.

## Random walks

`RandomWalk(index=..., by_region=..., prior_scale=...)`; a **list** of them is
summed, as R sums several `rw()` terms in one formula. An index of **-1** means
"this day gets no term from this walk" -- Python's spelling of R's `NA` in an
`rw(time = )` column, used to give a walk to only some groups.

Python stores a walk's **cumulative levels** as a Deterministic (`rw`, `rw_1`,
...); R reports its **increments**. The same arithmetic is therefore right in
one port and wrong in the other. Prefer deriving quantities from the posterior
`Rt` rather than from coefficients -- for a two-group model the ratio of the two
groups' `Rt` cancels any shared walk and depends on no parameterisation.

## Sampler settings are model-specific

`fit`/`fit_multilevel`/`fit_epidemia` default to `target_accept=0.95` and
`adaptation="low_rank"`, which wins on collinear-covariate posteriors (1.7x
Stan's ESS/second on the NPI model). That ranking does **not** always transfer:
the Flaxman reproduction needed `adaptation="diag"` (R-hat 1.17 -> 1.03), and
models whose trajectories saturate the tree depth need `maxdepth` above nutpie's
default of 10. Check the diagnostics rather than trusting the default.

`correlated=True` region effects need enough groups to support a full
covariance. With ~11 groups plus a per-group random walk it may not identify:
check `Sigma_chol` R-hat before trusting anything downstream, and prefer
`correlated=False` if it has not mixed.
